name: _GCC_specific_handler
prose: Windows SEH language-specific handler used by libunwind/mingw. Returns an EXCEPTION_DISPOSITION. (1) If ms_exc->ExceptionCode is STATUS_GCC_UNWIND: when the unwind flag marks a target unwind, it stores ms_exc->ExceptionInformation[3] into the second return register slot of disp->ContextRecord (Rdx on x86_64, R1 on arm, X1 on aarch64, nothing on other targets); in every case of this branch it returns ExceptionContinueSearch. (2) Else if the code is STATUS_GCC_THROW it takes the _Unwind_Exception from ExceptionInformation[0] and, when not unwinding and NumberParameters > 1, takes ctx and action from ExceptionInformation[1] and [2]; any other exception code returns ExceptionContinueSearch. (3) If ctx is still null it initialises a local cursor from disp->ContextRecord, attaches disp, sets the IP register to disp->ControlPc and derives action: not unwinding gives _UA_CLEANUP_PHASE|_UA_FORCE_UNWIND for a GCC throw with parameters and _UA_SEARCH_PHASE otherwise; unwinding gives _UA_CLEANUP_PHASE|_UA_HANDLER_FRAME when the throw's ExceptionInformation[1] equals frame, else _UA_CLEANUP_PHASE. (4) It calls the personality routine pers(1, action, exception_class, exc, ctx) and switches on the result: _URC_CONTINUE_UNWIND aborts if action has _UA_HANDLER_FRAME, else returns ExceptionContinueSearch; _URC_HANDLER_FOUND returns 4 (ExceptionExecuteHandler) for a GCC throw with parameters, aborts if the exception flags say unwinding, otherwise records frame in exc->private_[1] (and for a GCC throw sets NumberParameters = 4 and ExceptionInformation[1] = frame) and calls RtlUnwindEx, which does not return normally (the code aborts if it does); _URC_INSTALL_CONTEXT returns 4 for a GCC throw in the non-unwinding case with parameters, aborts during phase 1, otherwise stores the landing pad and return registers into exc->private_[2..3], turns ms_exc into a STATUS_GCC_UNWIND record and calls RtlUnwindEx (abort if it returns); any other result returns ExceptionContinueExecution. Only the STATUS_GCC_UNWIND branch writes through disp->ContextRecord directly.

Reviewer (r15) RIGHT: ContextRecord is written only at :103-107. Not read: __unw_init_seh/__unw_set_reg (whether they write through to the context record).

name: UnwindCursor<A, R>::stepWithSEHData
prose: Windows SEH step: calls RtlVirtualUnwind(UNW_FLAG_UHANDLER, ImageBase, ControlPc, FunctionEntry, ContextRecord, &HandlerData, &EstablisherFrame, NULL) on the cursor's _dispContext, storing the returned language handler in _dispContext.LanguageHandler (it may be null) and letting the call update ContextRecord, HandlerData and EstablisherFrame. Then it sets _info.lsda to the HandlerData pointer value (reinterpret_cast of the pointer, not the address of the field) and _info.handler to the address of __libunwind_seh_personality when LanguageHandler is non-null, or 0 otherwise. Its only return is UNW_STEP_SUCCESS; no error from RtlVirtualUnwind is checked. Precondition: _dispContext.ImageBase, ControlPc, FunctionEntry and ContextRecord have been set up by an earlier lookup.

name: UnwindCursor<A, R>::stepWithEHABI
prose: ARM EHABI step, compiled only for _LIBUNWIND_ARM_EHABI. _info.unwind_info is the encoded exception-handling-table word, not decoded data: it calls decode_eht_entry(unwind_info, &off, &len), which for the generic model (top bit clear) takes the unwind opcodes after the personality word with a length from the size byte, for the ARM compact model (top bit set) derives off/len from the format (SU16, LU16, LU32) and for any other format returns nullptr. It then calls _Unwind_VRS_Interpret(this as _Unwind_Context*, ehtp, off, len); if that returns anything other than _URC_CONTINUE_UNWIND the function returns UNW_STEP_END, otherwise UNW_STEP_SUCCESS. A null ehtp from decode_eht_entry is passed on to _Unwind_VRS_Interpret without a check here. Registers in the cursor are updated by the interpreter.

name: unwind_phase2_forced
prose: Forced-unwind phase 2 (libunwind UnwindLevel1.c). Initialises the cursor from uc itself (__unw_init_local), so the caller need not. It then loops while __unw_step_stage2(cursor) > 0: __unw_get_proc_info failure returns _URC_FATAL_PHASE2_ERROR; the stop function is called with action _UA_FORCE_UNWIND|_UA_CLEANUP_PHASE and any result other than _URC_NO_REASON returns _URC_FATAL_PHASE2_ERROR; if the frame has a personality routine it is called with that action: _URC_CONTINUE_UNWIND continues, _URC_INSTALL_CONTEXT calls __unw_phase2_resume(cursor, framesWalked) (normally does not return; if it does the loop continues) and any other result returns _URC_FATAL_PHASE2_ERROR. When the loop ends because __unw_step_stage2 returned 0 or negative (end of stack or step error; the code does not distinguish them), the stop function is called once more with _UA_END_OF_STACK added to the action, its result is ignored, and the function returns _URC_FATAL_PHASE2_ERROR. So every return is _URC_FATAL_PHASE2_ERROR; the early failure returns do not make the final stop call. Successful completion happens through the resume or the stop function transferring control.

name: operator<(const GHashCell &l, const GHashCell &r)
prose: Friend comparison of two GHashCell values: returns l.data < r.data, an unsigned 64-bit comparison of the packed cell words. The word layout is bit 63 = isItem, bits 62 to 32 = tpiSrcIdx + 1, bits 31 to 0 = ghashIdx, so cells with isItem == 0 compare less than cells with isItem == 1, then ties are ordered by (tpiSrcIdx + 1) and then by ghashIdx; an empty cell (data == 0) is the smallest. Pure function of its arguments, no side effects.

name: elf::createTaggedSymbols
prose: AArch64 MTE global-tagging pass over ctx.objectFiles; precondition (assert only) hasMemtag(ctx). Pass 1: for each ObjKind file and each non-null, non-discarded section of type SHT_AARCH64_MEMTAG_GLOBALS_STATIC, addTaggedSymbolReferences walks its relocations (a REL-format section reports an error but the walk continues over rels.relas): each relocation's target symbol that is not STT_OBJECT is skipped, a local symbol is marked tagged immediately, any other symbol has its count in a local DenseMap incremented; the section is then marked dead. Pass 2: for each Binary or Obj file and each symbol in it (declarations and definitions alike) that is STT_OBJECT and non-local and present in the map, if its remaining count is already 0 the entry is erased (the symbol is used by more declarations/definitions than tagged marks, so it stays untagged), otherwise the count is decremented. If the map is still non-empty and ctx.arg.writeAddends is set, an error about --apply-dynamic-relocs and MTE globals is reported (ErrAlways, processing continues). Finally every symbol still in the map is marked tagged (setIsTagged(true)); the code asserts its count is 0 (debug builds only). Locals are tagged unconditionally. No value is returned.

name: AArch64::relocate
prose: Applies one relocation to the bytes at loc, switching on rel.type with val the computed value. Range and alignment checks (checkInt, checkUInt, checkIntUInt, checkAlignment) only report an error through the linker's diagnostics when the value does not fit or is misaligned; they do not stop the write that follows. Groups: ABS16/PREL16 write 16 bits and ABS32/PREL32 write 32 bits (checkIntUInt), PLT32/GOTPCREL32 write 32 bits (checkInt). ABS64 writes 64 bits: val, or -rel.addend when rel.sym is tagged and the addend is negative or at least the symbol size. PREL64 writes 64 bits. AUTH_ABS64 writes a 32-bit value only if val fits in a signed 32-bit integer (isInt<32>); otherwise the location is left unchanged. ADR/ADRP page relocations check a 33-bit range (the _NC variant does not) and write the page value val >> 12; ADR_PREL_LO21 checks 21 bits. JUMP26 first overwrites the whole instruction word with 0x14000000 and then falls into CALL26, which checks a 28-bit range and writes the masked word offset. CONDBR19/LD_PREL_LO19-style relocations check 4-byte alignment and a 21-bit range. The LDSTn/LD64 low-12 relocations check alignment of n bytes and write the shifted 12-bit immediate; MOVW_UABS/SABS/PREL/TPREL relocations check ranges (not for the _NC and G3 variants) and write the 16-bit immediate from the matching bit group; TSTBR14 checks 16 bits; the TLSLE ADD relocations write the high 12 bits (checkUInt 24) or the low 12 bits; TLSDESC writes val to loc + 8. Any other rel.type reaches llvm_unreachable. Returns nothing.

name: AMDGPU::calcEFlags
prose: Computes the ELF e_flags for the output of an AMDGPU link from ctx.objectFiles. Returns 0 if there are no object files. Otherwise it reads the ABI version from the first object's header and dispatches: HSA_V2/V3 to calcEFlagsV3 (returns the first file's e_flags if all files have identical e_flags, else reports an error with ErrAlways and returns 0); HSA_V4/V5 to calcEFlagsV4 (compares mach across files, reports Err and returns 0 on mismatch, combines xnack and sramecc by the ANY/UNSUPPORTED rules, reporting Err and returning 0 on incompatibility, else returns mach|xnack|sramecc); HSA_V6 to calcEFlagsV6 (computes the V4 flags, then compares the generic version bits across files, reporting ErrAlways and returning 0 on mismatch, otherwise ORs the first file's generic version into the V4 result, so after a V4 incompatibility error the V4 value 0 still gets the generic version OR-ed in and a nonzero value can be returned); any other ABI version reports Err 'unknown abi version' and returns 0. Errors are reported through the diagnostics and execution continues to return a value.

name: X86_64::deleteFallThruJmpInsn
prose: Tries to delete a trailing direct jmp (5 bytes, opcode 0xe9) at the end of input section `is` when it falls through to the next section nextIS. Returns false without changes if nextIS is null, if the section is shorter than 5 bytes, if no live relocation (expr != R_NONE) sits at offset size-4, if the byte before that offset is not 0xe9, or if the relocation does not make the jump target equal to the start of nextIS (relocation must be PLT32, PC32 or PC8). If it is a fall-through jump it turns the relocation into R_NONE with offset 0, drops the last 5 bytes of the section, sets is.nopFiller and returns true. Otherwise, if the section is at least 11 bytes (5 + a 6-byte jcc), it looks for a relocation of a conditional jump right before the final jmp; the jcc opcode must be one of the known conditional types with an inverse, and its relocation must target nextIS; then it records a JumpInstrMod that inverts the conditional jump, copies the final jmp's expr/type/addend/symbol into the conditional jump's relocation, turns the final jmp's relocation into R_NONE, drops the last 5 bytes, sets nopFiller and returns true; any failed check on this second path returns false. Mutates is only on the true paths.

name: X86_64::relaxOnce
prose: One linker-relaxation pass for GOT-relative relocations. It computes minVA and maxVA over allocated output sections and returns false immediately if maxVA fits in an unsigned 31-bit value, or if maxVA-minVA fits in 31 bits and the output is PIC. Otherwise, for every relocation in executable output sections whose expr is R_RELAX_GOT_PC or R_RELAX_GOT_PC_NOPIC (the code asserts addend == -4 in debug builds) it computes the target virtual address with the matching addend; if the value fits in a signed 32-bit integer the relocation is left relaxed; otherwise, if the symbol has no aux entry yet (auxIdx == 0), it allocates one, adds a GOT entry and sets changed = true; in both of those not-fitting cases rel.expr is changed to R_GOT_PC. Returns changed, which is true only if at least one new GOT entry was created, so it can return false even though some relocations were converted to R_GOT_PC for symbols that already had an aux entry. The pass argument is not used.

name: EhReader::getFdeEncoding
prose: Parses a CIE and returns the FDE pointer encoding byte. It reads the augmentation via getAugmentation: skips 8 bytes, reads the version (must be 1 or 3, else an error is reported and an empty string results), reads the augmentation string, skips two LEB128 values and reads one byte (version 1) or skips a LEB128 (version 3). It then scans the augmentation characters: 'R' returns the next byte (0 if the buffer is empty, after an error report), 'z' skips a LEB128, 'L' reads a byte, 'P' calls skipAugP, 'B', 'S' and 'G' are ignored, and any other character reports an error and stops the scan. If no 'R' is reached it returns DW_EH_PE_absptr. Parse problems are reported through errOn (Err, non-fatal) and do not stop the scan, except the unknown-character case; so an error reported for an earlier 'P' or truncated field can still be followed by a returned 'R' byte. skipAugP reports an error for DW_EH_PE_aligned, for an unknown size, and also when the encoded size is greater than or equal to the remaining bytes.
note: lld/ELF/EhFrame.cpp:166-186 (callers' wrapper elf::getFdeEncoding at :134-136); getAugmentation :142-164, skipAugP :122-132. Reviewer (round 1) RIGHT: after a 'P' error the scan can still return a later 'R' byte. Reviewer (r15) RIGHT: skipAugP errors when size >= d.size() (:129). The mapping of i=7 to the EhReader method rather than the wrapper is from the name; wrapper behaves identically.

name: EhReader::hasLSDA
prose: Parses a CIE and returns true if its augmentation string contains 'L'. It uses getAugmentation (skip 8 bytes, version 1 or 3, read the string, skip two LEB128s, read a byte or skip a LEB128) and then scans the characters: 'L' returns true at once; 'z' skips a LEB128; 'P' calls skipAugP; 'R' reads a byte; 'B', 'S', 'G' are ignored; any other character reports an error and stops the scan; after the scan it returns false (also when getAugmentation failed with an empty string). Errors are reported through errOn (non-fatal) and do not stop the scan, so it can return true after reporting an error from an earlier 'P' or truncated field.

name: elf::hasLSDA
prose: Free function wrapper: constructs an EhReader over the section piece's section and data (EhReader(p.sec, p.data())) and returns EhReader::hasLSDA(). So it returns true if the CIE augmentation string of the piece contains 'L' before an unknown character stops the scan, false otherwise; parse problems are reported through the reader's non-fatal errOn diagnostics and do not by themselves change the result. No state of p is modified.

name: SharedFile::parse<ELFT>
prose: Parses a shared library (ELF DSO) input: collects dynamic tags and the versym/verdef/verneed section headers from the section table, then creates symbols. It allocates the symbols array (numSymbols entries) first. Early exits that do not process any symbol: SHT_GNU_versym present with numSymbols == 0 reports ErrAlways and returns; a DT_NEEDED or DT_SONAME value beyond the string table reports Err and returns (dtNeeded may already hold earlier entries); if another shared file with the same soname is already registered in ctx.symtab->soNames, this file's isNeeded is OR-ed into that earlier entry and the function returns without adding symbols; otherwise the file is appended to ctx.sharedFiles. It then parses verdefs and verneeds, parseGnuAndFeatures, builds a versym table (default VER_NDX_GLOBAL, filled from the versym section when present) and walks the global ELF symbols: a STB_LOCAL symbol in the global part gets Err and is skipped; an undefined symbol with a version other than local/global takes its name from the verneed table as name@version (a verneed index out of range reports ErrAlways and skips the symbol), is added as Undefined with isExported = true and, when it is not weak and unresolvedSymbolsInShlib is not Ignore, is pushed to requiredSymbols; a defined symbol whose version is VER_NDX_LOCAL or whose index is beyond verdefs is skipped (silently for MIPS _gp_disp, otherwise with ErrAlways); for the remaining defined symbols the unversioned SharedSymbol is added only when the symbol's version equals its index (i.e. the hidden bit is not set), and when the version is not VER_NDX_GLOBAL a second SharedSymbol named name@verdefname is added; both set dsoDefined and set versionId only when the symbol's file is this file. A hidden-version defined symbol therefore appears only under its versioned name. Returns nothing.

Reviewers (r15, r17) RIGHT: invalid DT_NEEDED/DT_SONAME and versym-without-symbols return immediately (:1539-1558), and hidden-version defined symbols are not added unversioned (:1657 condition ver == idx). Partly read: parseVerdefs, parseVerneed, parseGnuAndFeatures, getAlignment, and how `versym[i]` is bounds-checked (not checked in this function).

name: SymbolTable::scanVersionScript
prose: Applies the version-script patterns in ctx.arg.versionDefinitions to the symbol table, in three passes, then calls handleDynamicList(). Pass 1 (definitions in order): for each non-wildcard pattern of a version's non-local list it calls assignExactVersion with the version id/name, then again for the name `pattern@versionname` (includeNonDefault); non-wildcard local patterns do the same with VER_NDX_LOCAL and the name "local". If neither call found a symbol and ctx.arg.undefinedVersion is false, it reports Err (an error, not a warning): version script assignment ... failed: symbol not defined; so the error is suppressed when the `pattern@version` form matched even if the plain pattern matched nothing. Pass 2 (definitions in reverse order): every wildcard pattern other than "*" is passed to assignWildcardVersion (plain and with `@version` form), non-local with the version id and local with VER_NDX_LOCAL; no message is produced for an unmatched wildcard. Pass 3 (reverse order): patterns that are exactly "*" are assigned the same way; while no warning has been issued and the pattern is local or its version id is above VER_NDX_LOCAL, it warns once (Warn, sets asteriskReported) if '*' is used for both local and global scopes or for multiple version definitions, otherwise it records which scope has been seen. Nothing is returned; the result is stored in the symbols' versionId and versionScriptAssigned fields by the callees.

name: Writer<ELFT>::createPhdrs
prose: Builds the list of program headers (PhdrEntry) for one partition when the linker script has no PHDRS command. isMain is partNo == 1. Unless -n/-N: a PT_PHDR (main partition: the program headers output; otherwise the partition's program-headers section), a PT_INTERP for a .interp section of that partition, and, for the main partition, a first PT_LOAD containing the ELF header and program headers. It builds a PT_GNU_RELRO candidate from the partition's relro sections (ErrAlways if a relro section is not contiguous once the relro run has ended). The PT_LOAD loop visits every output section that needs a PT_LOAD: sections of other partitions are skipped, except that for the main partition a section of partition 255 gets its own PT_LOAD; for sections of this partition it computes newFlags (computeFlags), treats the flags as incompatible when they differ from the current load's flags (ignoring X when !W and singleRoRx, ignoring R when !W and singleXoRx), and extends the current PT_LOAD (OR-ing p_flags) only if one exists, the section is not the relro end, memRegion is the same, the LMA region matches (and the section has no lmaExpr) or the load's last section is the program headers, and either a SECTIONS command exists, the section is NOBITS, or the load's last section is not NOBITS; otherwise it starts a new PT_LOAD. Then it adds PT_TLS (if any TLS sections), PT_DYNAMIC, PT_GNU_RELRO (if non-empty), PT_GNU_EH_FRAME (when eh_frame and its header exist), OpenBSD-specific headers when the OSABI is OpenBSD and the sections exist, PT_GNU_STACK unless -z nognustack (RW, plus X for exec stack, p_memsz = stack size), PT_OPENBSD_NOBTCFI / PT_OPENBSD_WXNEEDED from options, PT_GNU_PROPERTY from .note.gnu.property, and PT_NOTE headers: consecutive allocatable SHT_NOTE sections of the partition share one PT_NOTE, a new one starts when there is none, when the section has an lmaExpr, or when its alignment differs from the previous note's last section; any other section in the partition ends the current PT_NOTE group. Returns the vector.

name: kmp_topology_t::filter_hw_subset
prose: Applies the user's KMP_HW_SUBSET to the detected topology and restricts the affinity masks accordingly. Returns false without filtering when no subset is set (__kmp_hw_subset null), when validation fails (each case issues a warning through KMP_AFF_WARNING or __kmp_msg: a requested layer type has no equivalent in the topology, two requested layers are equivalent, a count + offset exceeds the available count for a non-absolute subset, core attributes used on a non-hybrid machine with more than one attribute, core type and efficiency mixed, an invalid efficiency value, a core attribute count too large, an attribute missing or repeated), or when every hardware thread would be filtered out. Before validating it sorts and canonicalizes __kmp_hw_subset and rewrites each item's type to the equivalent topology type, so the subset is modified even on failure; a single core-attribute item on a non-hybrid machine is only warned about and ignored. Otherwise it allocates filtered_mask with KMP_CPU_ALLOC, copies __kmp_affin_fullMask into it, walks all hardware threads maintaining per-level sub-ids (absolute counters when the subset is absolute or core attributes are used) and clears a thread's os_id bit when any subset item rejects it (unknown id, sub-id outside [offset, offset+num), or core type/efficiency not listed), then calls restrict_to_mask(filtered_mask) and returns true. This function itself does not free filtered_mask.

name: __kmp_affinity_create_cpuinfo_map
prose: Builds __kmp_topology from /proc/cpuinfo-style data (platform-specific variants exist for AIX and others). Returns bool; *msg_id is set to kmp_i18n_null at entry and, on failure, to an error id. First it counts 'processor' records (and node_N id lines for the index range); false with NoProcRecords if none (:3266), TooManyProcRecords if more than __kmp_xproc, CantRewindCpuinfo if it cannot rewind the file. It allocates the threadInfo table (num_records+1 rows) and then parses line by line: a line longer than the buffer gives LongLineCpuinfo, a field line without ':' or number gives MissingValCpuinfo, a repeated field in one record gives DuplicateFieldCpuinfo (except where the code allows repeated processor lines on AArch64), a record end with num_avail == __kmp_xproc gives TooManyEntries, a record without a processor id gives MissingProcField; records whose os id is not in __kmp_affin_fullMask are skipped when affinity is capable. A package id missing for any record is filled from core siblings lists or gives MissingPhysicalIDField. It sorts the records, derives per-level counts, sets __kmp_nThreadsPerCore, nCoresPerPkg, nPackages and __kmp_ncores, and if affinity is not capable returns true at that point (with no __kmp_topology built; the code asserts affinity type is none). Otherwise it detects non-unique ids at a level (PhysicalIDsNotUnique, false), allocates __kmp_topology, fills each hardware thread, frees the temporary tables, sorts ids, fills missing thread ids, and if check_ids() fails deallocates __kmp_topology, sets it to nullptr, sets PhysicalIDsNotUnique and returns false; otherwise returns true. The temporary threadInfo rows are freed on the failure paths shown (CLEANUP_THREAD_INFO).

prose: Removes processor `proc` from an affinity mask given through mask (a pointer to a kmp_affin_mask_t pointer). name: ATOMIC_XCHG_WR(fixed4, wr, kmp_int32, 32, =, KMP_ARCH_X86)
prose: Generated function void __kmpc_atomic_fixed4_wr(ident_t *id_ref, int gtid, kmp_int32 *lhs, kmp_int32 rhs) (macro ATOMIC_XCHG_WR over ATOMIC_BEGIN). It asserts __kmp_init_serial in debug builds. When KMP_GOMP_COMPAT is compiled in, the GOMP flag (KMP_ARCH_X86, true only on 32-bit x86 builds) is non-zero and __kmp_atomic_mode == 2, it takes the generic atomic lock path (OP_GOMP_CRITICAL with op '=': get the gtid if needed, perform the store under the lock, return). Otherwise it performs KMP_XCHG_FIXED32(lhs, rhs), an atomic exchange whose old value is discarded, so *lhs becomes rhs. Returns nothing. Precondition: lhs points to a suitably aligned kmp_int32.

name: ATOMIC_XCHG_SWP(fixed4, kmp_int32, 32, KMP_ARCH_X86)
prose: Generated function kmp_int32 __kmpc_atomic_fixed4_swp(ident_t *id_ref, int gtid, kmp_int32 *lhs, kmp_int32 rhs) (macros ATOMIC_XCHG_SWP over ATOMIC_BEGIN_SWP). It asserts __kmp_init_serial in debug builds. When the GOMP flag (KMP_ARCH_X86) is non-zero and __kmp_atomic_mode == 2 it uses the generic lock (CRITICAL_SWP(0)): acquire the lock, old_value = *lhs, *lhs = rhs, release, return old_value. Otherwise old_value = KMP_XCHG_FIXED32(lhs, rhs), an atomic exchange, and it returns old_value. In both cases the returned value is the previous *lhs and *lhs equals rhs afterwards. Precondition: lhs points to an aligned kmp_int32.

name: ATOMIC_CRITICAL_CPT_WRK(cmplx4, add_cpt, kmp_cmplx32, +, 8c, 1)
prose: Generated function void __kmpc_atomic_cmplx4_add_cpt(ident_t *id_ref, int gtid, kmp_cmplx32 *lhs, kmp_cmplx32 rhs, kmp_cmplx32 *out, int flag). It asserts __kmp_init_serial in debug builds. When KMP_GOMP_COMPAT is compiled in, the flag argument 1 is set and __kmp_atomic_mode == 2, it takes the generic lock (LCK_ID 0) and does the capture below under it; otherwise it takes the 8c complex lock (ATOMIC_LOCK8c). Under the lock: if flag is non-zero, *lhs += rhs and *out = *lhs (the new value); if flag is zero, *out = *lhs (the old value) and then *lhs += rhs. The lock is released and the function returns void. It is a lock-based update, not a hardware atomic. Precondition: lhs and out point to valid kmp_cmplx32 objects; nothing in the code checks that they differ.

name: __kmp_init_hierarchical_barrier_thread
prose: Refreshes this thread's hierarchical-barrier state in thr_bar for team/nproc/tid and returns whether the team-related state changed. Let uninitialized = (thr_bar->team == NULL), team_changed, team_sz_changed (nproc differs from thr_bar->nproc) and tid_changed (tid differs from old_tid). If uninitialized or team_sz_changed it calls __kmp_get_hierarchy(nproc, thr_bar). If uninitialized, team_sz_changed or tid_changed it recomputes my_level and parent_tid (primary thread: my_level = depth-1, parent_tid = -1), offset, old_tid, wait_flag = KMP_BARRIER_NOT_WAITING, team and parent_bar (the parent_bar assignment indexes team->t.t_threads[parent_tid], which is index -1 for the primary thread; I did not verify that slot is valid). If uninitialized, team_changed or tid_changed it sets team and parent_bar again and sets the return value true. If uninitialized, team_sz_changed or tid_changed it sets nproc, recomputes leaf_kids (0 for level 0, clipped so tid + leaf_kids + 1 <= nproc) and leaf_state. It returns true exactly when uninitialized, team_changed or tid_changed was true; a pure team-size change returns false. Argument gtid is unused.

Reviewers (original, r15) RIGHT: true is also returned for uninitialized/tid_changed (:1338), and the nproc/leaf_kids/leaf_state/old_tid/wait_flag/my_level/parent_tid/offset updates are conditional (:1302-1354). Comment block above the function (:1286-1290) not otherwise used.

name: sqrt_newton_approx
prose: Approximates the square root of the unsigned 64-bit x with Newton's iteration in double precision: it starts with sqrt_new = (double)x and repeats sqrt_old = sqrt_new; sqrt_new = (sqrt_old + x / sqrt_old) / 2 while sqrt_old - sqrt_new > 0.1, then returns sqrt_new. The return value is the last iterate, which for x >= 1 comes from above (Newton iteration from x downwards) and, by the standard error bound for this iteration (derived, not tested), lies between sqrt(x) and sqrt(x) + 0.1 up to rounding error; for x == 1 it returns exactly 1.0. For x == 0 the first step computes 0.0/0.0, giving NaN, and the comparison with NaN is false, so it returns NaN. x is converted to double, so for x above 2^53 the input is rounded. No state is read or written.
note: openmp/runtime/src/kmp_collapse.cpp:1334-1342. Reviewers (round 1/2) RIGHT: x == 1 returns exactly sqrt(x), and x < 1 cannot occur for an unsigned argument (only 0 reaches that region).

name: __kmpc_end_serialized_parallel
prose: Leaves a serialized parallel region for the calling thread (gtid global_tid). If loc is non-null and has KMP_IDENT_AUTOPAR set it returns immediately without doing anything else. Otherwise it validates gtid, initialises the parallel runtime if needed, resumes from a soft pause, and if the thread's task team has found proxy tasks or hidden-helper tasks it waits on that task team. It asserts (KMP_ASSERT) that serial_team->t.t_serialized is non-zero. With OMPT enabled and the thread state not 'overhead' it issues implicit-task end and parallel-end callbacks and unlinks the lightweight task team. If the control-stack top's serial_nesting_level equals t_serialized it copies those ICVs back, pops and frees that entry. It pops the dispatch buffer stack (frees the top buffer), pops the task team node when t_serialized > 1, restores th_def_allocator, and decrements t_serialized. If t_serialized reaches 0 it restores the floating-point control state when saved (x87 and MXCSR), pops the current task, fires an OMPD breakpoint, restores th_team to the parent team, th_info.ds.ds_tid, the cached team nproc/master/serialized values and the dispatch pointer, marks the current task as executing, restores the task state and task team when tasking is enabled (not immediate-exec), and resets the root init mask when the team level is 0 and affinity reset is set; otherwise (still nested) it only traces. Finally it decrements serial_team->t.t_level, pops the parallel construct when the consistency check is on, and with OMPT sets the thread state to work_serial or work_parallel. Returns nothing.

Reviewers (original, r15) RIGHT: AUTOPAR early return is handled (:631), the task and control-stack restores are conditional (:686, :703, :710-761), and task state comes from the serial team (:748-752). Not read: callee bodies.

name: __kmp_dispatch_next<T>
prose: Returns non-zero if the calling thread was given another chunk of a dynamically scheduled loop, 0 when no more work remains. Outputs: *p_lb and *p_ub receive the chunk bounds, *p_st (when non-null in the serialized paths) the stride, and *p_last (when p_last is non-null) whether this is the last chunk, with the exceptions below. Serialized team (team->t.t_serialized): pr is the top dispatch buffer. If pr->u.p.tc == 0 the function sets *p_lb = *p_ub = 0, *p_st = 0 when non-null, pops the workshare when consistency checking is on, and returns 0 without touching *p_last. For a nomerge loop it hands out chunks of size parm1 by incrementing pr->u.p.count; when the chunk index is past the last it behaves like the tc == 0 case, otherwise it sets *p_lb/*p_ub (scaled by the stride), *p_last, *p_st and the ordered bounds when ordered. Otherwise (merged loop) it hands out the whole range once: sets tc = 0, *p_lb = lb, *p_ub = ub, last_upper, *p_last = TRUE when non-null and *p_st when non-null, and returns the earlier status (1). Active team: the status comes from the hierarchical scheduler when pr->flags.use_hier is set, otherwise from __kmp_dispatch_next_algorithm with the thread's team size and tid (p_st is passed through there without a null check in this function). If the status is 0, the shared num_done counter is atomically incremented, use_hier is cleared when hierarchical scheduling is compiled in, and the last thread to finish (num_done == team size - 1) resets the shared buffer: for static_steal it resets each thread's buffer steal_flag to UNUSED and frees 8-byte-type steal locks, then sets num_done = 0, iteration = 0, ordered_iteration = 0 only when the loop is ordered, and adds __kmp_dispatch_num_buffers to sh->buffer_index (it is advanced, not reset); every thread with status 0 pops the workshare when consistency checking is on and clears th_deo_fcn, th_dxo_fcn, th_dispatch_sh_current and th_dispatch_pr_current. If the status is non-zero and the chunk is the last, pr->u.p.last_upper = pr->u.p.ub. *p_last = last is written only when p_last is non-null and status != 0. In all paths OMPT dispatch/work-end callbacks and statistics are done before returning status.
note: openmp/runtime/src/kmp_dispatch.cpp:2180-2450 (serialized branch :2209-2323, active branch :2324-2428; status 0 reset :2347-2420). Reviewers RIGHT: reset is not on every 0 return (only last thread, :2365), buffer_index is incremented (:2403), ordered_iteration reset only if ordered (:2397-2399); r15 point about p_st: serialized paths check p_st != NULL (:2220, :2245, :2265, :2301) while the active path passes it on unchecked (:2343). Not read: __kmp_dispatch_next_algorithm, hierarchical next.

name: __kmp_dispatch_init_algorithm<T>
prose: Initialises the private dispatch info pr for a loop with bounds lb, ub, stride st, requested schedule and chunk, for team size nproc and thread tid. It records nomerge and ordered flags from the schedule value (ordered forces monotonic), resolves kmp_sch_static to __kmp_static, kmp_sch_runtime to the team's runtime schedule (chunk from the team's schedule, *cur_chunk updated when non-null), kmp_sch_guided_chunked to __kmp_guided, kmp_sch_auto to __kmp_auto, a non-positive explicit chunk to KMP_DEFAULT_CHUNK, kmp_sch_dynamic_chunked with non-monotonic to kmp_sch_static_steal, guided_analytical with more than 2^20 threads to guided_iterative (with a warning), and the runtime_simd cases to static_balanced_chunked or guided_simd (chunk multiplied by the team's chunk). It reports an error for st == 0 when the consistency check is on, computes the trip count tc from lb/ub/st (0 for an empty range), stores lb, ub, st, tc, count = 0, last_upper = ub + st, and for an active ordered loop resets the ordered bookkeeping. It then sets the per-schedule parameters in pr->u.p: static_steal splits chunks among threads and claims the buffer only when nproc > 1 and the chunk count is at least nproc, otherwise it switches to dynamic_chunked; static_balanced computes per-thread lb/ub; static_balanced_chunked always changes the schedule to static_greedy (parm1 = tc rounded up to chunk multiples per thread, or tc when nproc == 1); guided_simd/iterative falls back to dynamic_chunked when (2*chunk+1)*nproc >= tc and to static_greedy when nproc == 1; guided_analytical computes the cross-over point similarly (also falling back to dynamic_chunked or static_greedy); static_greedy and static_chunked/dynamic_chunked set parm1/parm2 (chunk clamped to 1..tc), trapezoidal sets parm1 to parm4, and any other schedule calls __kmp_fatal. Finally it stores the (possibly changed) schedule in pr->schedule. Returns nothing.
note: openmp/runtime/src/kmp_dispatch.cpp:184-897 (function end :897 `pr->schedule = schedule;`). Reviewers RIGHT: it can fall back to static_greedy (:657, :687) as well as dynamic_chunked (:575, :675, :705), and static_balanced_chunked unconditionally becomes static_greedy (:657). Partly read: the static_steal setup body (:440-570), static_balanced details (:584-650), guided analytical solver (:697-860); only schedule changes, parameter names and the fatal default were checked.

name: __kmp_dispatch_deo<UT>
prose: Template entry for an `ordered` region start in a dynamically scheduled loop; gtid is read from *gtid_ref (cid_ref unused). With __kmp_env_consistency_check on and pr->pushed_ws != ct_none it pushes a ct_ordered_in_pdo construct onto the consistency stack (this function contains no pop; any matching pop is elsewhere). If the team is not serialized: pr and sh come from the thread's dispatch current pointers; when KMP_GOMP_COMPAT is not defined and consistency checking is on, it reports CnsMultipleNesting if pr->ordered_bumped is set (that check only runs here in the non-serialized case); it then spin-waits (__kmp_wait with __kmp_ge) until sh->u.s.ordered_iteration >= pr->u.p.ordered_lower. In a serialized team it does nothing except the optional consistency push. Returns nothing.

name: __kmp_check_sync
prose: Consistency checking before entering a synchronization construct of type ct (OpenMP runtime consistency-check mode). It first grows the construct stack (__kmp_expand_cons_stack) when it is full, so stack storage may change even when no error is found. Then: for ct_ordered_in_parallel / ct_ordered_in_pdo, if the thread is not inside a worksharing construct (w_top <= p_top) it reports CnsBoundToWorksharing (or, with BUILD_PARALLEL_ORDERED, only asserts ct == ct_ordered_in_parallel); if inside one whose type is not ordered it reports CnsNoOrderedClause; and if the innermost sync construct (s_top above both p_top and w_top) is a critical, or an ordered with an ident flagged KMP_IDENT_KMPC, it reports CnsInvalidNesting. For ct_critical, only when lck is non-null and its owner is this thread (the same named critical is already held) it reports CnsNestingSameName with the matching stack entry. For ct_master / ct_masked / ct_reduce it reports CnsInvalidNesting when inside a worksharing construct, and for ct_reduce also when inside another sync construct. It does not check a critical nested inside a differently named critical or inside an ordered region. Returns nothing; errors go through __kmp_error_construct / __kmp_error_construct2, which I did not read.

Reviewers RIGHT: expand of the construct stack at :259-260 (state changes without an error); critical is checked only against same-owned lock (:296-319), ordered/critical nesting is checked only for the ordered cases (:278-295).
